description: Annotated, exact-set schema divergence baseline for scripts/check-migrator-parity.mjs. Every entry is an intentional, explained divergence between the canonical Swift migrator endpoint schema (OpenBurnBarCore/Sources/OpenBurnBarData) and a mirror surface. New divergences and stale entries both fail CI; keep reasons real.

Windows chat pipeline stores additional per-chat_message fields (backend/error/streaming metadata) that Mac keeps in transcriptPiecesJSON/attachments or in memory. Additive-only columns on a Windows-created DB; Mac decoders ignore unknown columns.

Windows chat pipeline stores additional per-chat_thread fields (backend/error/streaming metadata) that Mac keeps in transcriptPiecesJSON/attachments or in memory. Additive-only columns on a Windows-created DB; Mac decoders ignore unknown columns.

Windows provisions the conversation-transfer subset only: the sync/summary/word-count/key-* columns are Mac-side derived metadata the Windows read seams never touch. A Mac-transferred DB carries the full column set; fresh Windows DBs stay Windows-local until the sync engine is ported, so no Mac reader ever sees the narrow shape.
token_usage.syncedAt is Mac cloud-sync bookkeeping (v22 cross-device sync); the Windows port has no sync engine yet and its write seams never populate it. Add the column with the sync engine port.

Indexes are additive and can be created when the corresponding Windows query paths land; absence affects performance only, never correctness or data compatibility.

REAL NAMING DRIFT, semantically patched: Windows creates the same COALESCE(sourceDeviceId,'') + COALESCE(providerAccountID,'') unique index but under the v12-era name token_usage_unique_session_model_idx (see windows:extra-index entry). Uniqueness semantics match the Mac v28 endpoint; the NAME does not, so schema-hash byte-compat over a fresh Windows DB would fail. Rename on Windows next time the provisioner schema is revved.
